meta.title: My Autumn Book — Set 5
meta.subject: English Reading
meta.description: Challenge quiz testing inference, theme, and comparisons in 'My Autumn Book'.

questions.question: What is the main theme of 'My Autumn Book'?
options: Nature changes with the seasons, and we can observe and document these changes
Winter is the best season because it is very cold
Spiders are helpful garden animals
How to build a wooden shed in the backyard
questions.explanation: The story shows the narrator exploring the changing nature (leaves, animal behaviors) as summer transitions into autumn.

questions.question: We can infer that the weather becomes colder as autumn approaches.
questions.explanation: True. The chilly wind blowing and the narrator zipping their jacket show that the temperature is dropping.

questions.question: Why does the narrator empty their pack on their bedroom floor?
options: To look at and organize the autumn leaves they collected
To throw the leaves in the trash bin
To hide the leaves from their parents
To see if any spiders are inside
questions.explanation: The narrator spreads the collected leaves to decorate pages and make their autumn scrapbook.

questions.question: Caterpillars cocooning and squirrels burying treasure are signs that they are getting ready for spring.
questions.explanation: False. These are preparations for the cold winter, not spring.

questions.question: The story is written using rhymes (like shed/thread, wait/investigate). What does this do?
options: It makes the story read like a song or poem
It makes the story hard to understand
It explains how trees grow leaves
It tells the reader about different animals
questions.explanation: Rhymes give a poem a nice rhythm and flow, making it fun and song-like to read.

questions.question: We can infer that geese fly south because winter in their home will be too _______.
questions.explanation: Geese migrate south in autumn because they need to find warmer areas to survive winter.

questions.question: In the poem, how are the changing trees compared to people?
options: They dress up in colorful gowns, suits, and crowns
They run fast in the garden woods
They sing and chirrup like crickets
They fly south in formation
questions.explanation: The poem compares trees changing colors to dressing up (e.g., dogwood's crimson gown, oak's rust brown suit, aspen's gold crown).

questions.question: Sort these animal behaviors in autumn based on whether they focus on Gathering Food or Changing Bodies/Homes:
questions.explanation: Chipmunks and squirrels collect and store food. Caterpillars make cocoons (body change) and geese move to new homes (fly south).

questions.question: The woodpecker drumming on the tree agrees with the cicada's warning that summer is leaving.
questions.explanation: True. The woodpecker's rap-a-tap drumming is a sign of agreement that the weather is changing.

questions.question: Arrange the words to show what animals do in autumn:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'Animals prepare for the winter.' They store food or change their homes.

questions.question: Why is the book at the end of the story called 'My Autumn Book'?
options: Because the narrator made it using leaves and drawings collected during autumn
Because it teaches how to grow plants in spring
Because the narrator bought it at a store in autumn
Because it is a book about why summer is leaving
questions.explanation: The narrator spent the day collecting autumn leaves and objects, then arranged them on the pages of their scrapbook.

questions.question: When the crickets no longer sing and the outside world turns cold, we can infer that winter is _______.
questions.explanation: When crickets stop singing and the world turns white with cold, winter has finally arrived.

questions.question: Arrange the words to show when nature changes:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'Nature changes during each season.' We see this in plants and animals.

questions.question: The narrator zips up their jacket because they expect the weather to get warmer.
questions.explanation: False. The narrator zips their jacket because they feel a chilly wind, which means the weather is getting colder.

questions.question: Based on the story, how is a leaf scrapbook helpful to the narrator?
options: It preserves memories of the colorful autumn even when the outside world turns cold and white
It helps the narrator learn how to fly south with geese
It shows the spider how to weave a better web
It provides food for the chipmunk during the winter
questions.explanation: A scrapbook preserves the colors and memories of autumn so the narrator can enjoy them when the outside world is cold and colorless.
